---
name: karpathy-wiki
description: "Build and maintain a personal LLM Wiki: source files → compiled wiki → index. Supports Mode A (个人知识库/) and Mode B (workspace scan). Triggers: wiki, 知识库, 知识管理, 收录, 知识库初始化, 整理知识库, ingest, 知识入库, 搜索知识, query wiki, lint wiki, 查一下, 搜一下, 了解一下, look up, find out, search. MANDATORY: query local wiki BEFORE any web search."
---

# LLM Wiki Bootstrap for OpenClaw

## Global Concurrency Control (CRITICAL)

**NEVER fire more than 2 `task()` calls in a single response.** This is the #1 source of API rate-limit errors.

| Rule                 | Action                                                                    |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Max groups**       | Split work into **2 groups only**                                         |
| **Per group**        | **1 task at a time** — within each group, process items sequentially      |
| **Total concurrent** | Max 2 agents running (1 from Group A + 1 from Group B)                    |
| **Collect results**  | Wait for both agents to complete before firing the next pair              |
| **On error/timeout** | Immediately degrade: process remaining items 1 at a time (no more groups) |
| **NEVER**            | Do NOT fire 3, 5, 6, 8+ agents at once                                    |

**Why this matters**: Linting 10 wiki articles = 2 groups of 5 each, process 1+1 concurrently (one from Group A, one from Group B), NOT 10 agents. Ingesting 9 sources = 2 groups of [5, 4], NOT 9 agents.

**If you are about to fire more than 3 agents in one response: STOP. Batch them instead.**

---

## Core Philosophy

**Knowledge base = source files → compiled wiki → index**

Two modes, automatically detected:

### Mode A: 个人知识库 Mode (Preferred)

- `个人知识库/` — Your curated knowledge files. PDFs, docs, spreadsheets, text, images. The LLM reads from here, NEVER modifies existing files.
- `个人知识库/wiki/` — Synthesized, structured knowledge. Created and maintained by the skill.

### Mode B: Workspace Scan Mode (Fallback, when `个人知识库/` doesn't exist)

- **Entire workspace** becomes the knowledge source — but ONLY documentation/research files are scanned (see exclusion rules below).
- `wiki/` at workspace root — Skill-managed wiki directory.

**index** — Directory of everything. The "table of contents" for your wiki.

The LLM is not a database — it is a reasoning engine. The wiki exists so the LLM reads only relevant content at the right time.

## Directory Structure

### Mode A: 个人知识库 exists (Preferred)

```
├── 个人知识库/                    # User's knowledge base (DO NOT modify existing files)
│   ├── some-paper.pdf            # Source files live here
│   ├── report.xlsx               # The LLM reads these, never edits them
│   ├── notes.docx                # Any file type is fine
│   ├── article.md                # Text/markdown files too
│   ├── subfolder/                # Subfolders are scanned recursively
│   └── wiki/                     # Skill-managed wiki (CREATED by the skill)
│       ├── index.md              # Master index of all topics, entities, concepts
│       ├── log.md                # Log of all changes to the wiki
│       └── {slug}.md             # Individual wiki articles
```

### Mode B: Workspace Scan (Fallback — when `个人知识库/` doesn't exist)

```
├── wiki/                         # Skill-managed wiki at workspace root
│   ├── index.md
│   ├── log.md
│   └── {slug}.md
└── (scanning all workspace recursively, with exclusions below)
```

### Source Scan Exclusion Rules (APPLIES TO BOTH MODES)

When scanning any source directory (`个人知识库/` in Mode A, entire workspace in Mode B), these files and directories are **ALWAYS excluded**:

**Excluded directories** (language dependencies, artifacts):

- `node_modules/`, `.next/`, `.nuxt/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `out/`
- `__pycache__/`, `.venv/`, `venv/`, `env/`, `.env/`
- `.git/`, `.github/`, `.vscode/`, `.idea/`, `target/`
- `vendor/`, `.bundle/`, `coverage/`, `.cache/`, `tmp/`, `temp/`
- `gen/`, `generated/`, `.dart_tool/`, `.pub-cache/`, `.cargo/`
- `.terraform/`, `.serverless/`, `.wrangler/`
- `bin/`, `obj/`, `lib/` (for Dart/Flutter), `Pods/`, `.gradle/`

**Excluded file extensions** (code/script/config files — not knowledge content):

- Code: `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.py`, `.java`, `.go`, `.rs`, `.cpp`, `.c`, `.h`, `.hpp`, `.rb`, `.php`, `.swift`, `.kt`, `.scala`, `.cs`, `.fs`, `.sh`, `.bash`, `.zsh`, `.ps1`, `.bat`, `.cmd`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`
- Styles: `.css`, `.scss`, `.sass`, `.less`, `.styl`, `.pcss`, `.postcss`
- Config: `.json`, `.toml`, `.yml`, `.yaml`, `.ini`, `.cfg`, `.conf`
- Lockfiles: `.lock`, `.sum`, `.lock.json`, `.lock.yaml`, `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`
- Build artifacts: `.min.js`, `.min.css`, `.map`, `.chunk.js`, `.hot-update.js`

**Included** (these ARE knowledge content — in both modes):

- Documents: `.pdf`, `.docx`, `.doc`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`, `.xls`, `.rtf`, `.epub`, `.odt`, `.ods`, `.odp`
- Text: `.md`, `.txt`, `.csv`, `.text`
- Images (OCR-eligible): `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.webp`, `.bmp`, `.svg`

**Key rules**:

- All paths are relative to the workspace root
- Never modify existing user files — read only
- wiki/ (or 个人知识库/wiki/) is the only directory the skill creates and writes to
- Source files are always scanned recursively, excluding wiki/ subdirectory and exclusions above

---

## Document Extraction

When ingesting non-text files, the LLM **MUST** use the extraction script instead of reading raw bytes:

```bash
python {skill_dir}/scripts/doc_extractor.py "<filepath>"
python {skill_dir}/scripts/doc_extractor.py "<filepath>" --max-pages 50
python {skill_dir}/scripts/doc_extractor.py "<filepath>" --max-rows 10000
```

Where `{skill_dir}` is the directory containing this SKILL.md file.

**Supported formats**:
| Format | Extension | Library | Notes |
|--------|-----------|---------|-------|
| PDF | `.pdf` | PyMuPDF | `sort=True` for reading order, checks encryption |
| Excel | `.xlsx` | openpyxl | `read_only=True, data_only=True` |
| Excel (legacy) | `.xls` | xlrd | For older Excel files |
| Word | `.docx` | python-docx | Preserves headings and tables |
| PowerPoint | `.pptx` | python-pptx | Slides, tables, speaker notes, group shapes |
| RTF | `.rtf` | striprtf | Handles various codepages gracefully |
| EPUB | `.epub` | ebooklib + BeautifulSoup | Spine-ordered chapter extraction |
| OpenDocument Text | `.odt` | odfdo | Paragraphs, tables; markdown conversion fallback |
| OpenDocument Spreadsheet | `.ods` | odfdo | Table extraction with sheet names |
| OpenDocument Presentation | `.odp` | odfdo | Slide text from draw pages |
| Images (OCR) | `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.webp`, `.bmp` | EasyOCR | CJK+EN mixed content, `~ch_sim`+`en` models, paragraph=False |
| SVG | `.svg` | Inline text → svglib+reportlab → OCR fallback | Extract `<text>/<tspan>` elements first, rasterize then OCR if empty |

**Setup** (one-time): Install dependencies. **Use Chinese mirror if default pip timeout:**

```bash
# Try default first
pip install PyMuPDF openpyxl python-docx xlrd python-pptx striprtf ebooklib beautifulsoup4 lxml odfdo paddleocr paddlepaddle svglib reportlab

# LLM Wiki Bootstrap for OpenClaw

## Global Concurrency Control (CRITICAL)

**NEVER fire more than 2 `task()` calls in a single response.** This is the #1 source of API rate-limit errors.

| Rule                 | Action                                                                    |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Max groups**       | Split work into **2 groups only**                                         |
| **Per group**        | **1 task at a time** — within each group, process items sequentially      |
| **Total concurrent** | Max 2 agents running (1 from Group A + 1 from Group B)                    |
| **Collect results**  | Wait for both agents to complete before firing the next pair              |
| **On error/timeout** | Immediately degrade: process remaining items 1 at a time (no more groups) |
| **NEVER**            | Do NOT fire 3, 5, 6, 8+ agents at once                                    |

**Why this matters**: Linting 10 wiki articles = 2 groups of 5 each, process 1+1 concurrently (one from Group A, one from Group B), NOT 10 agents. Ingesting 9 sources = 2 groups of [5, 4], NOT 9 agents.

**If you are about to fire more than 3 agents in one response: STOP. Batch them instead.**

---

## Core Philosophy

**Knowledge base = source files → compiled wiki → index**

Two modes, automatically detected:

### Mode A: 个人知识库 Mode (Preferred)

- `个人知识库/` — Your curated knowledge files. PDFs, docs, spreadsheets, text, images. The LLM reads from here, NEVER modifies existing files.
- `个人知识库/wiki/` — Synthesized, structured knowledge. Created and maintained by the skill.

### Mode B: Workspace Scan Mode (Fallback, when `个人知识库/` doesn't exist)

- **Entire workspace** becomes the knowledge source — but ONLY documentation/research files are scanned (see exclusion rules below).
- `wiki/` at workspace root — Skill-managed wiki directory.

**index** — Directory of everything. The "table of contents" for your wiki.

The LLM is not a database — it is a reasoning engine. The wiki exists so the LLM reads only relevant content at the right time.

## Directory Structure

### Mode A: 个人知识库 exists (Preferred)

```
├── 个人知识库/                    # User's knowledge base (DO NOT modify existing files)
│   ├── some-paper.pdf            # Source files live here
│   ├── report.xlsx               # The LLM reads these, never edits them
│   ├── notes.docx                # Any file type is fine
│   ├── article.md                # Text/markdown files too
│   ├── subfolder/                # Subfolders are scanned recursively
│   └── wiki/                     # Skill-managed wiki (CREATED by the skill)
│       ├── index.md              # Master index of all topics, entities, concepts
│       ├── log.md                # Log of all changes to the wiki
│       └── {slug}.md             # Individual wiki articles
```

### Mode B: Workspace Scan (Fallback — when `个人知识库/` doesn't exist)

```
├── wiki/                         # Skill-managed wiki at workspace root
│   ├── index.md
│   ├── log.md
│   └── {slug}.md
└── (scanning all workspace recursively, with exclusions below)
```

### Source Scan Exclusion Rules (APPLIES TO BOTH MODES)

When scanning any source directory (`个人知识库/` in Mode A, entire workspace in Mode B), these files and directories are **ALWAYS excluded**:

**Excluded directories** (language dependencies, artifacts):

- `node_modules/`, `.next/`, `.nuxt/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `out/`
- `__pycache__/`, `.venv/`, `venv/`, `env/`, `.env/`
- `.git/`, `.github/`, `.vscode/`, `.idea/`, `target/`
- `vendor/`, `.bundle/`, `coverage/`, `.cache/`, `tmp/`, `temp/`
- `gen/`, `generated/`, `.dart_tool/`, `.pub-cache/`, `.cargo/`
- `.terraform/`, `.serverless/`, `.wrangler/`
- `bin/`, `obj/`, `lib/` (for Dart/Flutter), `Pods/`, `.gradle/`

**Excluded file extensions** (code/script/config files — not knowledge content):

- Code: `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.py`, `.java`, `.go`, `.rs`, `.cpp`, `.c`, `.h`, `.hpp`, `.rb`, `.php`, `.swift`, `.kt`, `.scala`, `.cs`, `.fs`, `.sh`, `.bash`, `.zsh`, `.ps1`, `.bat`, `.cmd`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`
- Styles: `.css`, `.scss`, `.sass`, `.less`, `.styl`, `.pcss`, `.postcss`
- Config: `.json`, `.toml`, `.yml`, `.yaml`, `.ini`, `.cfg`, `.conf`
- Lockfiles: `.lock`, `.sum`, `.lock.json`, `.lock.yaml`, `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`
- Build artifacts: `.min.js`, `.min.css`, `.map`, `.chunk.js`, `.hot-update.js`

**Included** (these ARE knowledge content — in both modes):

- Documents: `.pdf`, `.docx`, `.doc`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`, `.xls`, `.rtf`, `.epub`, `.odt`, `.ods`, `.odp`
- Text: `.md`, `.txt`, `.csv`, `.text`
- Images (OCR-eligible): `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.webp`, `.bmp`, `.svg`

**Key rules**:

- All paths are relative to the workspace root
- Never modify existing user files — read only
- wiki/ (or 个人知识库/wiki/) is the only directory the skill creates and writes to
- Source files are always scanned recursively, excluding wiki/ subdirectory and exclusions above

---

## Document Extraction

When ingesting non-text files, the LLM **MUST** use the extraction script instead of reading raw bytes:

```bash
python {skill_dir}/scripts/doc_extractor.py "<filepath>"
python {skill_dir}/scripts/doc_extractor.py "<filepath>" --max-pages 50
python {skill_dir}/scripts/doc_extractor.py "<filepath>" --max-rows 10000
```

Where `{skill_dir}` is the directory containing this SKILL.md file.

**Supported formats**:
| Format | Extension | Library | Notes |
|--------|-----------|---------|-------|
| PDF | `.pdf` | PyMuPDF | `sort=True` for reading order, checks encryption |
| Excel | `.xlsx` | openpyxl | `read_only=True, data_only=True` |
| Excel (legacy) | `.xls` | xlrd | For older Excel files |
| Word | `.docx` | python-docx | Preserves headings and tables |
| PowerPoint | `.pptx` | python-pptx | Slides, tables, speaker notes, group shapes |
| RTF | `.rtf` | striprtf | Handles various codepages gracefully |
| EPUB | `.epub` | ebooklib + BeautifulSoup | Spine-ordered chapter extraction |
| OpenDocument Text | `.odt` | odfdo | Paragraphs, tables; markdown conversion fallback |
| OpenDocument Spreadsheet | `.ods` | odfdo | Table extraction with sheet names |
| OpenDocument Presentation | `.odp` | odfdo | Slide text from draw pages |
| Images (OCR) | `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.webp`, `.bmp` | EasyOCR | CJK+EN mixed content, `~ch_sim`+`en` models, paragraph=False |
| SVG | `.svg` | Inline text → svglib+reportlab → OCR fallback | Extract `<text>/<tspan>` elements first, rasterize then OCR if empty |

**Setup** (one-time): Install dependencies. **Use Chinese mirror if default pip timeout:**

```bash

pip install PyMuPDF openpyxl python-docx xlrd python-pptx striprtf ebooklib beautifulsoup4 lxml odfdo paddleocr paddlepaddle svglib reportlab

# 旅行行程规划 Skill

## 概述

本 Skill 用于从零到一构建一份完整的旅行行程规划，涵盖需求调研、信息收集、行程编排、多格式输出全流程。核心原则是 **先收集再编排、先确认再输出**，避免一次性输出未经确认的行程。

## 工作流程

### Step 1: 需求调研（必须按顺序问）

#### 1.1 基础信息确认（必须主动询问）

如果用户没有主动给出，**必须逐项询问**以下信息：

```
- 目的地
- 出发和返回日期（含航班号和时间，若有）
- 人数
- 大交通方式（飞机/高铁/自驾等，从哪个城市出发）
- 住宿是否已定（若未定则进入住宿推荐环节）
```

> ⚠️ **原则：不要假设用户会主动给全信息。每缺失一项，主动追问一项。**

#### 1.2 旅行风格确认

主动询问用户 **两个维度** 的旅行偏好：

**维度一：内容偏好**
- 🍽️ **美食之旅** — 对吃的有追求，愿意为美食专程跑
- 🏛️ **景点打卡** — 著名景点必去，博物馆/地标/寺庙等
- 🛍️ **购物休闲** — 逛街买买买为主
- 🌿 **自然风光** — 海边/山川/公园放空
- 🤷 **混合型** — 什么都来一点

**维度二：节奏偏好**
- 🏃 **紧凑型** — 一天跑3-5个点，效率优先
- 🚶 **适中** — 一天2-3个点，有节奏感
- 🛀 **休闲型** — 一天1-2个点，随性放空

#### 1.3 已有素材收集

主动询问：**"你已经有收集或特别想去的地方吗？"**

- 如果有 → 全部记录下来，按类别整理（美食/景点/购物/住宿）
- 如果没有 → 根据目的地联网搜索热门推荐，提供多个选项供用户选择

#### 1.4 关键约束确认

- 预算范围（特别是住宿预算）
- 交通方式偏好（公共交通/包车/租车）
- 是否有特殊需求（超市购物、特定品牌、特定饮食需求）

---

### Step 2: 信息收集与整理

#### 2.1 用户自行收集的店铺/地点

当用户提供店铺或地点时，对 **每一家** 执行以下动作：

| 动作 | 说明 |
|:----|:------|
| 🔍 **搜索地址** | 用Tavily搜索完整地址、交通方式 |
| ⭐ **查询评分** | 记录Tabelog或Google评分 |
| ⏰ **确认营业时间** | 重点确认：营业时间、**定休日（翻译成星期几）** |
| 💰 **预算** | 人均消费范围 |
| 💳 **支付方式** | 是否现金only |
| 📝 **一句话描述** | 用户对这家店的评价或推荐理由 |
| 🎯 **标记优先级** | 哪些是"必去"，哪些是"备选" |

#### 2.2 信息组织方式

按 **区域** 和 **分类** 组织，便于后续排行程：

**分类标签：** 🍽️餐厅 / 🥖面包店 / ☕咖啡店 / 🛍️购物 / 🏛️景点 / 🐟水族馆 / 🏪超市

**区域划分：** 根据用户住宿地点，按步行圈/地铁圈分类

输出格式：**对比表格**（横向对比·一目了然）

```
| # | 店名 | 区域 | 分类 | 评分 | 距酒店 | 营业时间 | 休日 | 推荐 | 一句话描述 |
```

---

### Step 3: 住宿推荐（如用户未定）

#### 3.1 区域推荐

结合用户的旅行风格和行程分布，推荐1-2个最合适的住宿区域。推荐理由应包括：
- 交通便利性（到机场/主要景点的距离和耗时）
- 周边美食/购物密度
- 生活超市距离

#### 3.2 酒店推荐

按价格梯度分档推荐（经济/中档/品质），每家标注：
- 距最近车站的距离（徒步X分）
- 周边超市和便利店
- 特色亮点（景观/服务/积分体系）

#### 3.3 超市需求

**主动询问**用户是否需要附近有生活超市（买便当、零食、饮料等），这是容易被忽略但影响体验的关键因素。

---

### Step 4: 行程编排

#### 4.1 编排原则

| 原则 | 说明 |
|:----|:------|
| 🗺️ **按区域串点** | 同一天尽量安排在同一个区域，减少交通时间 |
| ⏰ **注意营业时间** | 先安排早关门的店，后安排晚关门的店 |
| 🚶 **标注交通方式** | 每段移动都要写清楚：方式+区间+时间 |
| ⚠️ **确认定休日** | 检查每家店的休日是否与行程日冲突 |
| 🛤️ **路线顺路** | 不走回头路，按地理顺序排列 |

#### 4.2 每日行程格式

采用 **三列表格** 格式：

```
| 时间 | 安排 | 交通 |
|:---:|:------|:------|
| 具体时间 | 事项描述（含店铺介绍）| 交通方式·区间·时间 |
```

每段移动都必须标注：
- 🚶 步行（标注分钟数）
- 🚇 地铁/🚃 JR/🚄 新干线（标注线路·区间·时间·费用）
- 🚐 包车/出租车

#### 4.3 营业时间冲突检查

对每一家店，**必须提前检查**它在你计划去的当天是否开门：
- 定休日是否撞上
- 营业时间是否覆盖你的计划到店时间
- 对冲突的店给出调整建议（改天去/换店）

---

### Step 5: 多格式输出

所有行程确认后，输出以下格式：

#### 5.0 天气信息标注

如果出发日期距离今天 **≤14天（2周内）**，在最终方案和行程图上需标注：

**天气信息来源：**
- 使用 `weather` skill 查询目的地每日天气
- 查询范围：行程覆盖的每一天

**标注位置：**
- Markdown文档：在每日行程标题旁标注 🌤️ 天气图标+气温（如 "🌤️ 24-28°C 晴"）
- 每日PDF：在顶部副标题旁标注天气
- 行程图Prompt：在prompt中加入天气描述（如 "Sunny 24°C"）

**天气信息格式示例：**
```
### 🛫 6/24（周三）— 抵达·浅草🌤️ 24-28°C 晴
```

> 注：如果出发日期 >14天，天气预报可能不准确，可标注"待临近查询天气"或跳过。

#### 5.1 Markdown 主文档（.md）

包含：
- 基本信息（航班/住宿/日期）
- 每日详细行程（含交通·时间·推荐）
- 美食清单对比表（按区域·分类）
- 购物指南
- 住宿信息

#### 5.2 Excel 文件（.xlsx）

- 美食清单（按区域分Sheet，含评分/地址/营业时间/距酒店距离）
- 购物指南（含超市/商场/品牌店）
- 可视化颜色区分（餐厅=黄色·面包=绿色·咖啡=蓝色）

**生成方式：** openpyxl + LibreOffice 转换PDF

#### 5.3 每日行程 PDF

每**每天**生成一份独立的 PDF，格式统一：

| 要素 | 规格 |
|:----|:------|
| 页面 | **横向A4**（landscape·297x210mm）|
| 字体 | Noto Sans CJK SC（思源黑体）|
| 颜色方案 | 蓝色标题·黄色餐饮·绿色交通·蓝色地铁 |
| 生成工具 | **WeasyPrint**（HTML→PDF）|

**PDF必须包含的列：** 时间·事项·交通方式·详细说明

#### 5.4 行程图（竖版+横版）

使用 `gpt-image-2` 模型生成可视化行程图：

**竖版规格：** 2048x2048（用于手机查看）
**横版规格：** 2048x1152（16:9·用于电脑/投屏）

Prompt要点：
- 描述当日行程的核心节点，按时间线排列
- 标注交通方式
- 包含食物/地点的小图标描述
- 指定整体色调和风格
- 标注"Chinese text"

#### 5.5 PDF 合并

- 竖版行程图 → 合并为 `行程图合集.pdf`（用img2pdf）
- 横版行程图 → 合并为 `行程图合集_横版.pdf`
- 6天每日PDF → 合并为 `日本行程全6日.pdf`

---

### Step 6: 交互节奏

| 阶段 | 节奏 |
|:----|:------|
| 📥 **收集阶段** | 用户扔店→你搜索整理→确认记录，快速迭代 |
| 🗓️ **排行程阶段** | **一天一天确认**：文字确认→用户点头→更新文档→生成PDF |
| 🎨 **出图阶段** | **两张两张或三张三张生成**，不要一次全跑 |
| ✅ **最终输出** | 全部确认后一次性完整输出 |

**关键原则：每次只确认一天的行程，不要一口气排完所有天。**

---

## 注意事项

### 非中文信息翻译原则

在整理信息时，**凡是遇到非中文的文字描述**（无论日文、英文、韩文等），都必须检查并翻译成中文：

| 场景 | 原文示例 | 翻译后 |
|:----|:---------|:-------|
| 星期/日期 | 月曜日·火曜·水曜·木曜·金曜·土曜·日曜 | 周一·周二·周三·周四·周五·周六·周日 |
| 休息日表述 | 定休日：毎週水曜日 | 定休日：每周三 |
| 地址 | 東京都中央区銀座8-13-1 | 保留原文（日本地址用原汁原味好找路）|
| 营业时间 | 11:00～22:00（L.O.21:00）| 保留数字，翻译注释：L.O.=最后点单 |
| 店铺类型 | とんかつ·うなぎ·お好み焼き | 炸猪排·鳗鱼·大阪烧 |
| 菜品名 | 極み厚切り牛たん定食 | 極み厚切り牛たん定食（顶级厚切牛舌套餐）|
| 英文描述 | Closed on Sundays and public holidays | 周日及节假日休息 |

> ⚠️ **地址和店名保留原文**（方便导航和问路），但注释要加中文说明。
> ⚠️ 时间数字、价格数字、电话号码保留原样不翻译。

### 时间管理
- 图片生成（gpt-image-2）耗时较长，每张约1-3分钟
- PDF生成（WeasyPrint）约5-10秒
- Excel生成约2-3秒

### 中文支持
- PDF字体：Noto Sans CJK SC（系统思源黑体）
- 避免在PDF中使用emoji（CJK字体不含emoji字形）
- Excel使用Arial即可

### 工具链
- **PDF生成：** WeasyPrint（HTML→PDF）
- **Excel生成：** openpyxl
- **图片生成：** gpt-image-2（zzz4ai endpoint）
- **PDF合并：** img2pdf
- **搜索：** Tavily（地址/评分/营业时间）

### 常见陷阱
- 日本店铺的定休日用日文写的（水曜=周三·木曜=周四），必须翻译成星期几
- "不定休"=没有固定休息日，但可能临时关门
- 很多老店只收现金，要提前标注
- 商场里的餐厅随商场营业时间，不一定是独立营业时间

# EvoMind Paper Scan

`evomind-paper-scan` is an OpenClaw-compatible academic review skill. It combines:

- whole-paper 29-dimension quality review;
- paper/source-data/table consistency review;
- numeric anomaly scanning for data tables using `paperconan`;
- cautious research-integrity risk language;
- EvoMind-branded Markdown and Word internal reports.

## Branding and Attribution

Use these exact defaults unless the user overrides them:

- Overall review process: `EvoMind Paper-Data-Scan v1.0（EvoMind 自研审查流程）`
- Review institution: `EvoMind 学术质量审查实验室`
- Document number: `EM-REP-20260602-001`
- Confidentiality: `内部资料`
- Header: `EvoMind 内部审查报告`
- Footer: `EvoMind 学术质量审查实验室 | 内部资料`
- Sign-off warning: `AI判断不能作为最终结果，需人工复核`

Data audit attribution is mandatory:

> 数据审核/数字异常扫描部分使用 paperconan 开源工具，项目地址：https://github.com/zixixr/paperconan。EvoMind 尊重并保留原作者工具署名；EvoMind Paper-Data-Scan v1.0 指本机构的整合审查流程、报告规范和人工复核框架。

Do not describe `paperconan` as EvoMind self-developed. EvoMind owns the integrated review workflow and report format, while the data numeric scan component must credit paperconan.

## Required Review Order

1. Confirm inputs: paper PDF/DOCX, source-data folder, supplementary files, desired language, and output folder.
2. Read the whole paper first. Identify title, author/year, field, research question, methods, tables, figures, claims, datasets, and source-data availability.
3. Complete the 29-dimension review using `references/29-dimension-checklist.md`.
4. Build a figure/table/source-data review queue.
5. Run numeric scan on source-data/supplementary tables when available. Use paperconan and preserve attribution.
6. Interpret numeric findings only through paper text, captions, methods, sample structure, and plausible benign explanations. Never treat scanner severity as final judgment.
7. Produce Markdown reports, auxiliary summaries, and a DOCX internal report if requested.

## Direct Script Usage

From the skill folder:

```powershell
python .\scripts\run_evomind_paper_scan.py --paper "<paper.pdf>" --source-data "<source data folder>" --out-dir ".\reports" --title "<paper title>" --docx
```

If no source-data folder exists, omit `--source-data`; the script will scan the PDF table extraction where possible and mark source data as missing.

The script creates:

```text
reports/
  <paper-title>/
    paper_data_scan_zh.md
    paper_data_scan_en.md
    auxiliary/
      numeric_scan_summary_zh.md
      numeric_scan_summary_en.md
      source_data_inventory_zh.md
      source_data_inventory_en.md
    audit/
      scan.json
      REPORT.md
      report.html
    EvoMind_内部审查报告.docx
```

## Output Rules

The main report must include:

- report metadata and EvoMind branding;
- paper identity and reviewed files;
- whole-paper baseline;
- 29-dimension quality matrix;
- source-data inventory;
- numeric scan summary with paperconan attribution;
- integrated findings comparing paper text, tables, figures, source data, and scanner output;
- limitations and next manual checks;
- red sign-off warning in DOCX.

## Integrity Language

Never conclude misconduct, fraud, fabrication, plagiarism, or author intent from scanner output alone. Use language such as:

- `possible fabrication risk`;
- `requires raw data confirmation`;
- `confirmed inconsistency`;
- `scanner finding with plausible benign explanation`;
- `source data unavailable, reproducibility limited`.

## Related Files

- `OPENCLAW.md`: OpenClaw installation and usage guide.
- `skill.yaml`: OpenClaw package metadata.
- `security.json`: local-only permissions and data-handling policy.
- `scripts/run_evomind_paper_scan.py`: direct runnable pipeline.
- `scripts/generate_evomind_word_report.py`: DOCX generator.
- `references/29-dimension-checklist.md`: required review matrix.
- `references/numeric-scan-interpretation.md`: scanner interpretation guardrails.

# PDF Processing Guide

## Overview

This guide covers essential PDF processing operations using Python libraries and command-line tools. For advanced features, JavaScript libraries, and detailed examples, see REFERENCE.md. If you need to fill out a PDF form, read FORMS.md and follow its instructions.

## Quick Start

```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

# Read a PDF
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
print(f"Pages: {len(reader.pages)}")

# Extract text
text = ""
for page in reader.pages:
    text += page.extract_text()
```

## Python Libraries

### pypdf - Basic Operations

#### Merge PDFs
```python
from pypdf import PdfWriter, PdfReader

writer = PdfWriter()
for pdf_file in ["doc1.pdf", "doc2.pdf", "doc3.pdf"]:
    reader = PdfReader(pdf_file)
    for page in reader.pages:
        writer.add_page(page)

with open("merged.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

#### Split PDF
```python
reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
for i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):
    writer = PdfWriter()
    writer.add_page(page)
    with open(f"page_{i+1}.pdf", "wb") as output:
        writer.write(output)
```

#### Extract Metadata
```python
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
meta = reader.metadata
print(f"Title: {meta.title}")
print(f"Author: {meta.author}")
print(f"Subject: {meta.subject}")
print(f"Creator: {meta.creator}")
```

#### Rotate Pages
```python
reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

page = reader.pages[0]
page.rotate(90)  # Rotate 90 degrees clockwise
writer.add_page(page)

with open("rotated.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

### pdfplumber - Text and Table Extraction

#### Extract Text with Layout
```python
import pdfplumber

with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    for page in pdf.pages:
        text = page.extract_text()
        print(text)
```

#### Extract Tables
```python
with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):
        tables = page.extract_tables()
        for j, table in enumerate(tables):
            print(f"Table {j+1} on page {i+1}:")
            for row in table:
                print(row)
```

#### Advanced Table Extraction
```python
import pandas as pd

with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    all_tables = []
    for page in pdf.pages:
        tables = page.extract_tables()
        for table in tables:
            if table:  # Check if table is not empty
                df = pd.DataFrame(table[1:], columns=table[0])
                all_tables.append(df)

# Combine all tables
if all_tables:
    combined_df = pd.concat(all_tables, ignore_index=True)
    combined_df.to_excel("extracted_tables.xlsx", index=False)
```

### reportlab - Create PDFs

#### Basic PDF Creation
```python
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas

c = canvas.Canvas("hello.pdf", pagesize=letter)
width, height = letter

# Add text
c.drawString(100, height - 100, "Hello World!")
c.drawString(100, height - 120, "This is a PDF created with reportlab")

# Add a line
c.line(100, height - 140, 400, height - 140)

# Save
c.save()
```

#### Create PDF with Multiple Pages
```python
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
from reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak
from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet

doc = SimpleDocTemplate("report.pdf", pagesize=letter)
styles = getSampleStyleSheet()
story = []

# Add content
title = Paragraph("Report Title", styles['Title'])
story.append(title)
story.append(Spacer(1, 12))

body = Paragraph("This is the body of the report. " * 20, styles['Normal'])
story.append(body)
story.append(PageBreak())

# Page 2
story.append(Paragraph("Page 2", styles['Heading1']))
story.append(Paragraph("Content for page 2", styles['Normal']))

# Build PDF
doc.build(story)
```

#### Subscripts and Superscripts

**IMPORTANT**: Never use Unicode subscript/superscript characters (₀₁₂₃₄₅₆₇₈₉, ⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹) in ReportLab PDFs. The built-in fonts do not include these glyphs, causing them to render as solid black boxes.

Instead, use ReportLab's XML markup tags in Paragraph objects:
```python
from reportlab.platypus import Paragraph
from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet

styles = getSampleStyleSheet()

# Subscripts: use <sub> tag
chemical = Paragraph("H<sub>2</sub>O", styles['Normal'])

# Superscripts: use <super> tag
squared = Paragraph("x<super>2</super> + y<super>2</super>", styles['Normal'])
```

For canvas-drawn text (not Paragraph objects), manually adjust font the size and position rather than using Unicode subscripts/superscripts.

## Command-Line Tools

### pdftotext (poppler-utils)
```bash
# Extract text
pdftotext input.pdf output.txt

# Extract text preserving layout
pdftotext -layout input.pdf output.txt

# Extract specific pages
pdftotext -f 1 -l 5 input.pdf output.txt  # Pages 1-5
```

### qpdf
```bash
# Merge PDFs
qpdf --empty --pages file1.pdf file2.pdf -- merged.pdf

# Split pages
qpdf input.pdf --pages . 1-5 -- pages1-5.pdf
qpdf input.pdf --pages . 6-10 -- pages6-10.pdf

# Rotate pages
qpdf input.pdf output.pdf --rotate=+90:1  # Rotate page 1 by 90 degrees

# Remove password
qpdf --password=*** --decrypt encrypted.pdf decrypted.pdf
```

### pdftk (if available)
```bash
# Merge
pdftk file1.pdf file2.pdf cat output merged.pdf

# Split
pdftk input.pdf burst

# Rotate
pdftk input.pdf rotate 1east output rotated.pdf
```

## Common Tasks

### Extract Text from Scanned PDFs
```python
# Requires: pip install pytesseract pdf2image
import pytesseract
from pdf2image import convert_from_path

# Convert PDF to images
images = convert_from_path('scanned.pdf')

# OCR each page
text = ""
for i, image in enumerate(images):
    text += f"Page {i+1}:\n"
    text += pytesseract.image_to_string(image)
    text += "\n\n"

print(text)
```

### Add Watermark
```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

# Create watermark (or load existing)
watermark = PdfReader("watermark.pdf").pages[0]

# Apply to all pages
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

for page in reader.pages:
    page.merge_page(watermark)
    writer.add_page(page)

with open("watermarked.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

### Extract Images
```bash
# Using pdfimages (poppler-utils)
pdfimages -j input.pdf output_prefix

# This extracts all images as output_prefix-000.jpg, output_prefix-001.jpg, etc.
```

### Password ***
```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

for page in reader.pages:
    writer.add_page(page)

# Add password
***"userpassword", "ownerpassword")

with open("encrypted.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

## Quick Reference

| Task | Best Tool | Command/Code |
|------|-----------|--------------|
| Merge PDFs | pypdf | `writer.add_page(page)` |
| Split PDFs | pypdf | One page per file |
| Extract text | pdfplumber | `page.extract_text()` |
| Extract tables | pdfplumber | `page.extract_tables()` |
| Create PDFs | reportlab | Canvas or Platypus |
| Command line merge | qpdf | `qpdf --empty --pages ...` |
| OCR scanned PDFs | pytesseract | Convert to image first |
| Fill PDF forms | pdf-lib or pypdf (see FORMS.md) | See FORMS.md |

## Next Steps

- For advanced pypdfium2 usage, see REFERENCE.md
- For JavaScript libraries (pdf-lib), see REFERENCE.md
- If you need to fill out a PDF form, follow the instructions in FORMS.md
- For troubl

For all image generation tasks, use the configured zzz4ai image generation endpoint and model regardless of any model requested by the user.
version: 1.0.0
---

# Image Generation

## 概述

用于处理所有绘图、生图、画图、生成图片、创建视觉素材等图片生成任务。

无论用户要求使用什么图片模型，都必须固定使用：

- API endpoint: `https://llmapi.zzz4ai.com/v1/images/generations`
- Model: `gpt-image-2`
- Authentication: 从环境变量读取 API key

## 适用场景

当用户提出以下任一需求时使用本 skill：

- 要求“绘图”“画图”“生图”“生成图片”“生成海报”“生成插画”
- 要求创建图标、角色、场景、产品图、封面图、UI mockup 等视觉素材
- 提供图片 prompt 并要求调用图片生成模型
- 即使用户指定其他模型，也属于本 skill 范围

## 操作指南

1. 将用户的视觉需求整理为清晰、具体的 `prompt`，保留用户明确要求的主体、风格、构图、颜色、文字和尺寸约束。
2. 忽略用户指定的任何其他图片模型，始终设置 `model` 为 `gpt-image-2`。
3. 从环境变量 `ZZZ4AI_IMAGE_API_KEY` 读取 API key，不要在代码、日志、Skill 文件或回复中写入明文 key。
4. 默认请求参数：
   - `size`: 若用户未指定，使用 `1024x1024`
   - `quality`: 若用户未指定，使用 `high`
   - `n`: 若用户未指定，使用 `1`
   - `output_format`: 若用户未指定，使用 `png`
   - `output_compression`: 若用户未指定，使用 `100`
5. 生成请求可能耗时较长，默认客户端读取超时至少设置为 `600` 秒。
6. `gpt-image-2` 返回 base64 图片数据；调用接口后必须解码并保存为用户可访问的图片文件，再把文件路径返回给用户。

## 参数约束

- `prompt`: 必填，图片提示词。
- `model`: 必填，始终为 `gpt-image-2`。
- `n`: 可选，生成图片数量，范围 `1` 到 `10`。
- `size`: 可选，默认按接口能力可为 `auto`，本 skill 默认使用 `1024x1024`；宽高都必须是 16 像素的倍数，单边最高 `3840`，宽高比最高 `3:1`，像素总数范围 `655360` 到 `8294400`。
- `quality`: 可选，支持 `low`、`medium`、`high`。
- `output_format`: 可选，支持 `png`、`jpeg`。
- `output_compression`: 可选，范围 `0` 到 `100`；`0` 为不压缩，`100` 为最大压缩。

推荐尺寸：`1024x1024`、`1024x1536`、`1536x1024`、`2048x2048`、`2048x1152`、`2160x3840`。

## 响应处理

响应通常包含：

- `created`: 请求创建时间的 Unix 时间戳。
- `data`: 图片结果数组；`gpt-image-2` 返回 `b64_json` base64 数据。
- `usage`: token 用量信息，若接口返回则可用于调试或统计。
- `error`: 错误对象，包含 `code`、`message`、`param` 等字段。

## 图片落盘流程

默认使用以下流程把模型返回的 base64 转成用户可访问的图片文件：

1. 从 `payload["data"][i]["b64_json"]` 读取 base64 字符串。
2. 如果字符串以 `data:` 开头，使用 `partition(",")` 取逗号后的实际 base64 内容。
3. 根据 `output_format` 决定文件扩展名：`png` 保存为 `.png`，`jpeg` 保存为 `.jpg`。
4. 保存到当前 workspace 下的可访问目录，例如 `outputs/images/`。
5. 多图请求按序号保存，例如 `image_001.png`、`image_002.png`。
6. 返回保存后的本地文件路径，不返回 base64 字符串。

最高效的默认实现是直接用 Python 标准库 `base64.b64decode()` 解码后写入二进制文件。不要再经过 PIL、OpenCV 或额外转码，除非用户明确要求后处理；这样可以避免无意义的 CPU 开销和图像质量变化。

## 请求模板

```bash
curl --max-time 600 https://llmapi.zzz4ai.com/v1/images/generations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ZZZ4AI_IMAGE_API_KEY}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-image-2",
    "prompt": "a beautiful flower",
    "size": "1024x1024",
    "quality": "high",
    "output_format": "png",
    "output_compression": 100
  }'
```

## Python 示例

```python
import base64
import os
from pathlib import Path

import requests


def generate_image(
    prompt: str,
    output_dir: str = "outputs/images",
    filename_stem: str = "image",
    size: str = "1024x1024",
    quality: str = "high",
    n: int = 1,
    output_format: str = "png",
    output_compression: int = 100,
    timeout: int = 600,
) -> list[str]:
    api_key = ***"ZZZ4AI_IMAGE_API_KEY"]
    response = requests.post(
        "https://llmapi.zzz4ai.com/v1/images/generations",
        headers={
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}",
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
        },
        json={
            "model": "gpt-image-2",
            "prompt": prompt,
            "size": size,
            "quality": quality,
            "n": n,
            "output_format": output_format,
            "output_compression": output_compression,
        },
        timeout=timeout,
    )
    response.raise_for_status()
    payload = response.json()

    target_dir = Path(output_dir)
    target_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    extension = "jpg" if output_format == "jpeg" else output_format

    output_paths = []
    for index, item in enumerate(payload["data"], start=1):
        image_b64 = item["b64_json"]
        if image_b64.startswith("data:"):
            _, _, image_b64 = image_b64.partition(",")

        output_path = target_dir / f"{filename_stem}_{index:03d}.{extension}"
        output_path.write_bytes(base64.b64decode(image_b64))
        output_paths.append(str(output_path))

    return output_paths
```

## 注意事项

- 不要把 API key 写入仓库；只通过 `ZZZ4AI_IMAGE_API_KEY` 环境变量读取。
- 不要因为用户要求其他模型而切换模型；所有绘图相关任务统一使用 `gpt-image-2`。
- 如果环境变量不存在，先提示用户配置 `ZZZ4AI_IMAGE_API_KEY`，不要要求用户在聊天中粘贴密钥。
- 若用户请求不符合安全或合规要求，应拒绝或要求修改 prompt。

# Image Generation

## 概述

用于处理所有绘图、生图、画图、生成图片、创建视觉素材等图片生成任务。

无论用户要求使用什么图片模型，都必须固定使用：

- API endpoint: `https://llmapi.zzz4ai.com/v1/images/generations`
- Model: `gpt-image-2`
- Authentication: 从环境变量读取 API key

## 适用场景

当用户提出以下任一需求时使用本 skill：

- 要求“绘图”“画图”“生图”“生成图片”“生成海报”“生成插画”
- 要求创建图标、角色、场景、产品图、封面图、UI mockup 等视觉素材
- 提供图片 prompt 并要求调用图片生成模型
- 即使用户指定其他模型，也属于本 skill 范围

## 操作指南

1. 将用户的视觉需求整理为清晰、具体的 `prompt`，保留用户明确要求的主体、风格、构图、颜色、文字和尺寸约束。
2. 忽略用户指定的任何其他图片模型，始终设置 `model` 为 `gpt-image-2`。
3. 从环境变量 `ZZZ4AI_IMAGE_API_KEY` 读取 API key，不要在代码、日志、Skill 文件或回复中写入明文 key。
4. 默认请求参数：
   - `size`: 若用户未指定，使用 `1024x1024`
   - `quality`: 若用户未指定，使用 `high`
   - `n`: 若用户未指定，使用 `1`
   - `output_format`: 若用户未指定，使用 `png`
   - `output_compression`: 若用户未指定，使用 `100`
5. 生成请求可能耗时较长，默认客户端读取超时至少设置为 `600` 秒。
6. `gpt-image-2` 返回 base64 图片数据；调用接口后必须解码并保存为用户可访问的图片文件，再把文件路径返回给用户。

## 参数约束

- `prompt`: 必填，图片提示词。
- `model`: 必填，始终为 `gpt-image-2`。
- `n`: 可选，生成图片数量，范围 `1` 到 `10`。
- `size`: 可选，默认按接口能力可为 `auto`，本 skill 默认使用 `1024x1024`；宽高都必须是 16 像素的倍数，单边最高 `3840`，宽高比最高 `3:1`，像素总数范围 `655360` 到 `8294400`。
- `quality`: 可选，支持 `low`、`medium`、`high`。
- `output_format`: 可选，支持 `png`、`jpeg`。
- `output_compression`: 可选，范围 `0` 到 `100`；`0` 为不压缩，`100` 为最大压缩。

推荐尺寸：`1024x1024`、`1024x1536`、`1536x1024`、`2048x2048`、`2048x1152`、`2160x3840`。

## 响应处理

响应通常包含：

- `created`: 请求创建时间的 Unix 时间戳。
- `data`: 图片结果数组；`gpt-image-2` 返回 `b64_json` base64 数据。
- `usage`: token 用量信息，若接口返回则可用于调试或统计。
- `error`: 错误对象，包含 `code`、`message`、`param` 等字段。

## 图片落盘流程

默认使用以下流程把模型返回的 base64 转成用户可访问的图片文件：

1. 从 `payload["data"][i]["b64_json"]` 读取 base64 字符串。
2. 如果字符串以 `data:` 开头，使用 `partition(",")` 取逗号后的实际 base64 内容。
3. 根据 `output_format` 决定文件扩展名：`png` 保存为 `.png`，`jpeg` 保存为 `.jpg`。
4. 保存到当前 workspace 下的可访问目录，例如 `outputs/images/`。
5. 多图请求按序号保存，例如 `image_001.png`、`image_002.png`。
6. 返回保存后的本地文件路径，不返回 base64 字符串。

最高效的默认实现是直接用 Python 标准库 `base64.b64decode()` 解码后写入二进制文件。不要再经过 PIL、OpenCV 或额外转码，除非用户明确要求后处理；这样可以避免无意义的 CPU 开销和图像质量变化。

## 请求模板

```bash
curl --max-time 600 https://llmapi.zzz4ai.com/v1/images/generations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ZZZ4AI_IMAGE_API_KEY}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-image-2",
    "prompt": "a beautiful flower",
    "size": "1024x1024",
    "quality": "high",
    "output_format": "png",
    "output_compression": 100
  }'
```

## Python 示例

```python
import base64
import os
from pathlib import Path

import requests


def generate_image(
    prompt: str,
    output_dir: str = "outputs/images",
    filename_stem: str = "image",
    size: str = "1024x1024",
    quality: str = "high",
    n: int = 1,
    output_format: str = "png",
    output_compression: int = 100,
    timeout: int = 600,
) -> list[str]:
    api_key = ***"ZZZ4AI_IMAGE_API_KEY"]
    response = requests.post(
        "https://llmapi.zzz4ai.com/v1/images/generations",
        headers={
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}",
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
        },
        json={
            "model": "gpt-image-2",
            "prompt": prompt,
            "size": size,
            "quality": quality,
            "n": n,
            "output_format": output_format,
            "output_compression": output_compression,
        },
        timeout=timeout,
    )
    response.raise_for_status()
    payload = response.json()

    target_dir = Path(output_dir)
    target_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    extension = "jpg" if output_format == "jpeg" else output_format

    output_paths = []
    for index, item in enumerate(payload["data"], start=1):
        image_b64 = item["b64_json"]
        if image_b64.startswith("data:"):
            _, _, image_b64 = image_b64.partition(",")

        output_path = target_dir / f"{filename_stem}_{index:03d}.{extension}"
        output_path.write_bytes(base64.b64decode(image_b64))
        output_paths.append(str(output_path))

    return output_paths
```

## 注意事项

- 不要把 API key 写入仓库；只通过 `ZZZ4AI_IMAGE_API_KEY` 环境变量读取。
- 不要因为用户要求其他模型而切换模型；所有绘图相关任务统一使用 `gpt-image-2`。
- 如果环境变量不存在，先提示用户配置 `ZZZ4AI_IMAGE_API_KEY`，不要要求用户在聊天中粘贴密钥。
- 若用户请求不符合安全或合规要求，应拒绝或要求修改 prompt。

# PDF Processing Guide

## Overview

This guide covers essential PDF processing operations using Python libraries and command-line tools. For advanced features, JavaScript libraries, and detailed examples, see REFERENCE.md. If you need to fill out a PDF form, read FORMS.md and follow its instructions.

## Quick Start

```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

# Read a PDF
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
print(f"Pages: {len(reader.pages)}")

# Extract text
text = ""
for page in reader.pages:
    text += page.extract_text()
```

## Python Libraries

### pypdf - Basic Operations

#### Merge PDFs

```python
from pypdf import PdfWriter, PdfReader

writer = PdfWriter()
for pdf_file in ["doc1.pdf", "doc2.pdf", "doc3.pdf"]:
    reader = PdfReader(pdf_file)
    for page in reader.pages:
        writer.add_page(page)

with open("merged.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

#### Split PDF

```python
reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
for i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):
    writer = PdfWriter()
    writer.add_page(page)
    with open(f"page_{i+1}.pdf", "wb") as output:
        writer.write(output)
```

#### Extract Metadata

```python
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
meta = reader.metadata
print(f"Title: {meta.title}")
print(f"Author: {meta.author}")
print(f"Subject: {meta.subject}")
print(f"Creator: {meta.creator}")
```

#### Rotate Pages

```python
reader = PdfReader("input.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

page = reader.pages[0]
page.rotate(90)  # Rotate 90 degrees clockwise
writer.add_page(page)

with open("rotated.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

### pdfplumber - Text and Table Extraction

#### Extract Text with Layout

```python
import pdfplumber

with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    for page in pdf.pages:
        text = page.extract_text()
        print(text)
```

#### Extract Tables

```python
with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):
        tables = page.extract_tables()
        for j, table in enumerate(tables):
            print(f"Table {j+1} on page {i+1}:")
            for row in table:
                print(row)
```

#### Advanced Table Extraction

```python
import pandas as pd

with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    all_tables = []
    for page in pdf.pages:
        tables = page.extract_tables()
        for table in tables:
            if table:  # Check if table is not empty
                df = pd.DataFrame(table[1:], columns=table[0])
                all_tables.append(df)

# Combine all tables
if all_tables:
    combined_df = pd.concat(all_tables, ignore_index=True)
    combined_df.to_excel("extracted_tables.xlsx", index=False)
```

### reportlab - Create PDFs

#### Basic PDF Creation

```python
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas

c = canvas.Canvas("hello.pdf", pagesize=letter)
width, height = letter

# Add text
c.drawString(100, height - 100, "Hello World!")
c.drawString(100, height - 120, "This is a PDF created with reportlab")

# Add a line
c.line(100, height - 140, 400, height - 140)

# Save
c.save()
```

#### Create PDF with Multiple Pages

```python
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
from reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak
from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet

doc = SimpleDocTemplate("report.pdf", pagesize=letter)
styles = getSampleStyleSheet()
story = []

# Add content
title = Paragraph("Report Title", styles['Title'])
story.append(title)
story.append(Spacer(1, 12))

body = Paragraph("This is the body of the report. " * 20, styles['Normal'])
story.append(body)
story.append(PageBreak())

# Page 2
story.append(Paragraph("Page 2", styles['Heading1']))
story.append(Paragraph("Content for page 2", styles['Normal']))

# Build PDF
doc.build(story)
```

#### Subscripts and Superscripts

**IMPORTANT**: Never use Unicode subscript/superscript characters (₀₁₂₃₄₅₆₇₈₉, ⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹) in ReportLab PDFs. The built-in fonts do not include these glyphs, causing them to render as solid black boxes.

Instead, use ReportLab's XML markup tags in Paragraph objects:

```python
from reportlab.platypus import Paragraph
from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet

styles = getSampleStyleSheet()

# Subscripts: use <sub> tag
chemical = Paragraph("H<sub>2</sub>O", styles['Normal'])

# Superscripts: use <super> tag
squared = Paragraph("x<super>2</super> + y<super>2</super>", styles['Normal'])
```

For canvas-drawn text (not Paragraph objects), manually adjust font the size and position rather than using Unicode subscripts/superscripts.

## Command-Line Tools

### pdftotext (poppler-utils)

```bash
# Extract text
pdftotext input.pdf output.txt

# Extract text preserving layout
pdftotext -layout input.pdf output.txt

# Extract specific pages
pdftotext -f 1 -l 5 input.pdf output.txt  # Pages 1-5
```

### qpdf

```bash
# Merge PDFs
qpdf --empty --pages file1.pdf file2.pdf -- merged.pdf

# Split pages
qpdf input.pdf --pages . 1-5 -- pages1-5.pdf
qpdf input.pdf --pages . 6-10 -- pages6-10.pdf

# Rotate pages
qpdf input.pdf output.pdf --rotate=+90:1  # Rotate page 1 by 90 degrees

# Remove password
qpdf --password=*** --decrypt encrypted.pdf decrypted.pdf
```

### pdftk (if available)

```bash
# Merge
pdftk file1.pdf file2.pdf cat output merged.pdf

# Split
pdftk input.pdf burst

# Rotate
pdftk input.pdf rotate 1east output rotated.pdf
```

# Requires: pip install pytesseract pdf2image

from pdf2image import convert_from_path

# Convert PDF to images
images = convert_from_path('scanned.pdf')

# OCR each page
text = ""
for i, image in enumerate(images):
    text += f"Page {i+1}:\n"
    text += pytesseract.image_to_string(image)
    text += "\n\n"

print(text)
```

### Add Watermark

```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

# Create watermark (or load existing)
watermark = PdfReader("watermark.pdf").pages[0]

# Apply to all pages
reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
writer = PdfWriter()

for page in reader.pages:
    page.merge_page(watermark)
    writer.add_page(page)

with open("watermarked.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)
```

### Extract Images

```bash
# Using pdfimages (poppler-utils)
pdfimages -j input.pdf output_prefix

# This extracts all images as output_prefix-000.jpg, output_prefix-001.jpg, etc.
```

for page in reader.pages:
    writer.add_page(page)

with open("encrypted.pdf", "wb") as output:
    writer.write(output)

# Deep Research

You are an expert researcher who provides thorough, well-cited analysis by synthesizing information from multiple perspectives.

## When to Apply

Use this skill when:

- Conducting in-depth research on a topic
- Synthesizing information from multiple sources
- Creating research summaries with proper citations
- Analyzing different viewpoints and perspectives
- Identifying key findings and trends
- Evaluating the quality and credibility of sources

## Research Process

Follow this systematic approach:

### 1. **Clarify the Research Question**

- What exactly needs to be researched?

## Executive Summary

Intermittent fasting (IF) shows promising benefits for weight loss and metabolic health based on current research, though long-term effects remain under study. Evidence supports its safety for most healthy adults, with certain populations requiring medical supervision [1][2].

## Key Findings

- **Weight Loss**: IF produces similar weight loss to calorie restriction (5-8% body weight over 12 weeks), with potentially better adherence [1]
- **Metabolic Health**: May improve insulin sensitivity by 20-31% and reduce inflammation markers [2]
- **Longevity**: Animal studies show promise; human long-term data is limited [3]
- **Safety**: Not recommended for pregnant women, diabetics without supervision, or those with eating disorder history [4]

## Detailed Analysis

### Weight Management

Studies comparing IF to traditional calorie restriction show similar weight loss outcomes. The main advantage appears to be adherence - many people find time-restricted eating easier to maintain than calorie counting [1]. Typical results show 5-8% body weight loss over 12-16 weeks.

Common IF protocols:

- **16:8** - 16 hours fasting, 8-hour eating window
- **5:2** - Normal eating 5 days, restricted calories 2 days
- **Alternate day** - Alternating between fasting and eating days

### Metabolic Effects

Research indicates improvements in several biomarkers [2]:

- Fasting insulin levels decreased 20-31%
- Blood pressure reductions (3-8 mmHg systolic)
- Inflammatory marker (CRP) reductions
- Improved lipid profiles in some studies

However, individual responses vary significantly. Some people show dramatic improvements while others see minimal changes.

### Potential Mechanisms

Several explanations for observed benefits:

1. **Caloric restriction** - IF naturally reduces total calories
2. **Circadian alignment** - Eating during daytime hours aligns with metabolism
3. **Autophagy** - Cellular cleanup processes activated during fasting
4. **Hormetic stress** - Mild stress that improves adaptation

### Safety Considerations

While generally safe for healthy adults, certain groups should avoid IF or proceed with medical supervision [4]:

- Pregnant or breastfeeding women
- People with diabetes (risk of hypoglycemia)
- History of eating disorders
- Children and adolescents
- Those taking medications requiring food

Common side effects during adaptation (1-2 weeks):

- Hunger and irritability
- Headaches
- Fatigue
- Difficulty concentrating

## Areas of Consensus

- IF is as effective as traditional diets for weight loss
- Short-term safety is established for healthy adults
- Individual results vary considerably
- Not a magic solution - overall diet quality matters

## Areas of Debate

- **Optimal fasting window**: Research shows benefits across different protocols
- **Long-term sustainability**: Most studies are 8-24 weeks; need multi-year data
- **Superiority to other diets**: Unclear if benefits exceed other healthy eating patterns
- **Muscle preservation**: Some concern about muscle loss, but studies show mixed results

## Sources

[1] Varady KA, et al. "Clinical application of intermittent fasting for weight loss." *Nature Reviews Endocrinology*, 2022. (Systematic review, high credibility)

[2] de Cabo R, Mattson MP. "Effects of Intermittent Fasting on Health, Aging, and Disease." *New England Journal of Medicine*, 2019. (Peer-reviewed, authoritative review)

[3] Longo VD, Panda S. "Fasting, Circadian Rhythms, and Time-Restricted Feeding in Healthy Lifespan." *Cell Metabolism*, 2016. (Mechanistic research, preliminary human data)

[4] Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics. "Position on Intermittent Fasting." 2022. (Professional organization guidelines)

## Gaps and Further Research

- **Long-term studies** (5+ years) needed for sustained effects
- **Different populations** - effects across ages, sexes, ethnicities
- **Optimization** - best fasting windows, meal timing, macronutrient composition
- **Clinical applications** - specific diseases or conditions that benefit most

# XLSX creation, editing, and analysis

## Overview

A user may ask you to create, edit, or analyze the contents of an .xlsx file. You have different tools and workflows available for different tasks.

## Important Requirements

**LibreOffice Required for Formula Recalculation**: You can assume LibreOffice is installed for recalculating formula values using the `scripts/recalc.py` script. The script automatically configures LibreOffice on first run, including in sandboxed environments where Unix sockets are restricted (handled by `scripts/office/soffice.py`)

## Reading and analyzing data

### Data analysis with pandas
For data analysis, visualization, and basic operations, use **pandas** which provides powerful data manipulation capabilities:

```python
import pandas as pd

# Read Excel
df = pd.read_excel('file.xlsx')  # Default: first sheet
all_sheets = pd.read_excel('file.xlsx', sheet_name=None)  # All sheets as dict

# Analyze
df.head()      # Preview data
df.info()      # Column info
df.describe()  # Statistics

# Write Excel
df.to_excel('output.xlsx', index=False)
```

## Excel File Workflows

## CRITICAL: Use Formulas, Not Hardcoded Values

**Always use Excel formulas instead of calculating values in Python and hardcoding them.** This ensures the spreadsheet remains dynamic and updateable.

### ❌ WRONG - Hardcoding Calculated Values
```python
# Bad: Calculating in Python and hardcoding result
total = df['Sales'].sum()
sheet['B10'] = total  # Hardcodes 5000

# Bad: Computing growth rate in Python
growth = (df.iloc[-1]['Revenue'] - df.iloc[0]['Revenue']) / df.iloc[0]['Revenue']
sheet['C5'] = growth  # Hardcodes 0.15

# Bad: Python calculation for average
avg = sum(values) / len(values)
sheet['D20'] = avg  # Hardcodes 42.5
```

### ✅ CORRECT - Using Excel Formulas
```python
# Good: Let Excel calculate the sum
sheet['B10'] = '=SUM(B2:B9)'

# Good: Growth rate as Excel formula
sheet['C5'] = '=(C4-C2)/C2'

# Good: Average using Excel function
sheet['D20'] = '=AVERAGE(D2:D19)'
```

This applies to ALL calculations - totals, percentages, ratios, differences, etc. The spreadsheet should be able to recalculate when source data changes.

## Common Workflow
1. **Choose tool**: pandas for data, openpyxl for formulas/formatting
2. **Create/Load**: Create new workbook or load existing file
3. **Modify**: Add/edit data, formulas, and formatting
4. **Save**: Write to file
5. **Recalculate formulas (MANDATORY IF USING FORMULAS)**: Use the scripts/recalc.py script
   ```bash
   python scripts/recalc.py output.xlsx
   ```
6. **Verify and fix any errors**: 
   - The script returns JSON with error details
   - If `status` is `errors_found`, check `error_summary` for specific error types and locations
   - Fix the identified errors and recalculate again
   - Common errors to fix:
     - `#REF!`: Invalid cell references
     - `#DIV/0!`: Division by zero
     - `#VALUE!`: Wrong data type in formula
     - `#NAME?`: Unrecognized formula name

### Creating new Excel files

```python
# Using openpyxl for formulas and formatting
from openpyxl import Workbook
from openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill, Alignment

wb = Workbook()
sheet = wb.active

# Add data
sheet['A1'] = 'Hello'
sheet['B1'] = 'World'
sheet.append(['Row', 'of', 'data'])

# Add formula
sheet['B2'] = '=SUM(A1:A10)'

# Formatting

sheet['A1'].fill = PatternFill('solid', start_color='FFFF00')
sheet['A1'].alignment = Alignment(horizontal='center')

# Column width
sheet.column_dimensions['A'].width = 20

wb.save('output.xlsx')
```

sheet.delete_cols(3)  # Delete column 3

```

# EvoMind Paper Scan

`evomind-paper-scan` is an OpenClaw-compatible academic review skill. It combines:

- whole-paper 29-dimension quality review;
- paper/source-data/table consistency review;
- numeric anomaly scanning for data tables using `paperconan`;
- cautious research-integrity risk language;
- EvoMind-branded Markdown and Word internal reports.

## Branding

Use these exact defaults unless the user overrides them:

- Overall review process: `EvoMind Paper-Data-Scan v1.0（EvoMind 自研审查流程）`
- Review institution: `EvoMind 学术质量审查实验室`
- Document number: `EM-REP-20260602-001`
- Confidentiality: `内部资料`
- Header: `EvoMind 内部审查报告`
- Footer: `EvoMind 学术质量审查实验室 | 内部资料`
- Sign-off warning: `AI判断不能作为最终结果，需人工复核`

Use a concise component label in professional reports:

- Data audit component: `paperconan v0.5.0`

## Required Review Order

1. Confirm inputs: paper PDF/DOCX, source-data folder, supplementary files, desired language, and output folder.
2. Read the whole paper first. Identify title, author/year, field, research question, methods, tables, figures, claims, datasets, and source-data availability.
3. Complete the 29-dimension review using `references/29-dimension-checklist.md`.
4. Build a figure/table/source-data review queue.
5. Run numeric scan on source-data/supplementary tables when available.
6. Interpret numeric findings only through paper text, captions, methods, sample structure, and plausible benign explanations. Never treat scanner severity as final judgment.
7. Produce Markdown reports, auxiliary summaries, and DOCX/PDF internal reports if requested.

## Direct Script Usage

From the skill folder:

```powershell
python .\scripts\run_evomind_paper_scan.py --paper "<paper.pdf>" --source-data "<source data folder>" --out-dir ".\reports" --title "<paper title>" --docx --pdf
```

If no source-data folder exists, omit `--source-data`; the script will scan the PDF table extraction where possible and mark source data as missing.

The script creates:

```text
reports/
  <paper-title>/
    paper_data_scan_zh.md
    paper_data_scan_en.md
    auxiliary/
      numeric_scan_summary_zh.md
      numeric_scan_summary_en.md
      source_data_inventory_zh.md
      source_data_inventory_en.md
    audit/
      scan.json
      REPORT.md
      report.html
    EvoMind_内部审查报告.docx
    EvoMind_内部审查报告.pdf
```

## Output Rules

The main report must include:

- report metadata and EvoMind branding;
- paper identity and reviewed files;
- whole-paper baseline;
- 29-dimension quality matrix;
- source-data inventory;
- numeric scan summary;
- integrated findings comparing paper text, tables, figures, source data, and scanner output;
- limitations and next manual checks;
- red sign-off warning in DOCX.

## Integrity Language

Never conclude misconduct, fraud, fabrication, plagiarism, or author intent from scanner output alone. Use language such as:

- `possible fabrication risk`;
- `requires raw data confirmation`;
- `confirmed inconsistency`;
- `scanner finding with plausible benign explanation`;
- `source data unavailable, reproducibility limited`.

# LLM Wiki Bootstrap for OpenClaw

## Global Concurrency Control (CRITICAL)

**NEVER fire more than 2 `task()` calls in a single response.** This is the #1 source of API rate-limit errors.

| Rule                 | Action                                                                    |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Max groups**       | Split work into **2 groups only**                                         |
| **Per group**        | **1 task at a time** — within each group, process items sequentially      |
| **Total concurrent** | Max 2 agents running (1 from Group A + 1 from Group B)                    |
| **Collect results**  | Wait for both agents to complete before firing the next pair              |
| **On error/timeout** | Immediately degrade: process remaining items 1 at a time (no more groups) |
| **NEVER**            | Do NOT fire 3, 5, 6, 8+ agents at once                                    |

**Why this matters**: Linting 10 wiki articles = 2 groups of 5 each, process 1+1 concurrently (one from Group A, one from Group B), NOT 10 agents. Ingesting 9 sources = 2 groups of [5, 4], NOT 9 agents.

**If you are about to fire more than 3 agents in one response: STOP. Batch them instead.**

---

## Core Philosophy

**Knowledge base = source files → compiled wiki → index**

Two modes, automatically detected:

### Mode A: 个人知识库 Mode (Preferred)

- `个人知识库/` — Your curated knowledge files. PDFs, docs, spreadsheets, text, images. The LLM reads from here, NEVER modifies existing files.
- `个人知识库/wiki/` — Synthesized, structured knowledge. Created and maintained by the skill.

### Mode B: Workspace Scan Mode (Fallback, when `个人知识库/` doesn't exist)

- **Entire workspace** becomes the knowledge source — but ONLY documentation/research files are scanned (see exclusion rules below).
- `wiki/` at workspace root — Skill-managed wiki directory.

**index** — Directory of everything. The "table of contents" for your wiki.

The LLM is not a database — it is a reasoning engine. The wiki exists so the LLM reads only relevant content at the right time.

## Directory Structure

### Mode A: 个人知识库 exists (Preferred)

```
├── 个人知识库/                    # User's knowledge base (DO NOT modify existing files)
│   ├── some-paper.pdf            # Source files live here
│   ├── report.xlsx               # The LLM reads these, never edits them
│   ├── notes.docx                # Any file type is fine
│   ├── article.md                # Text/markdown files too
│   ├── subfolder/                # Subfolders are scanned recursively
│   └── wiki/                     # Skill-managed wiki (CREATED by the skill)
│       ├── index.md              # Master index of all topics, entities, concepts
│       ├── log.md                # Log of all changes to the wiki
│       └── {slug}.md             # Individual wiki articles
```

### Mode B: Workspace Scan (Fallback — when `个人知识库/` doesn't exist)

```
├── wiki/                         # Skill-managed wiki at workspace root
│   ├── index.md
│   ├── log.md
│   └── {slug}.md
└── (scanning all workspace recursively, with exclusions below)
```

### Source Scan Exclusion Rules (APPLIES TO BOTH MODES)

When scanning any source directory (`个人知识库/` in Mode A, entire workspace in Mode B), these files and directories are **ALWAYS excluded**:

**Excluded directories** (language dependencies, artifacts):

- `node_modules/`, `.next/`, `.nuxt/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `out/`
- `__pycache__/`, `.venv/`, `venv/`, `env/`, `.env/`
- `.git/`, `.github/`, `.vscode/`, `.idea/`, `target/`
- `vendor/`, `.bundle/`, `coverage/`, `.cache/`, `tmp/`, `temp/`
- `gen/`, `generated/`, `.dart_tool/`, `.pub-cache/`, `.cargo/`
- `.terraform/`, `.serverless/`, `.wrangler/`
- `bin/`, `obj/`, `lib/` (for Dart/Flutter), `Pods/`, `.gradle/`

**Excluded file extensions** (code/script/config files — not knowledge content):

- Code: `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.py`, `.java`, `.go`, `.rs`, `.cpp`, `.c`, `.h`, `.hpp`, `.rb`, `.php`, `.swift`, `.kt`, `.scala`, `.cs`, `.fs`, `.sh`, `.bash`, `.zsh`, `.ps1`, `.bat`, `.cmd`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`
- Styles: `.css`, `.scss`, `.sass`, `.less`, `.styl`, `.pcss`, `.postcss`
- Config: `.json`, `.toml`, `.yml`, `.yaml`, `.ini`, `.cfg`, `.conf`
- Lockfiles: `.lock`, `.sum`, `.lock.json`, `.lock.yaml`, `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`
- Build artifacts: `.min.js`, `.min.css`, `.map`, `.chunk.js`, `.hot-update.js`

**Included** (these ARE knowledge content — in both modes):

- Documents: `.pdf`, `.docx`, `.doc`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`, `.xls`, `.rtf`, `.epub`, `.odt`, `.ods`, `.odp`
- Text: `.md`, `.txt`, `.csv`, `.text`
- Images (OCR-eligible): `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.webp`, `.bmp`, `.svg`

**Key rules**:

- All paths are relative to the workspace root
- Never modify existing user files — read only
- wiki/ (or 个人知识库/wiki/) is the only directory the skill creates and writes to
- Source files are always scanned recursively, excluding wiki/ subdirectory and exclusions above

---

## Document Extraction

When ingesting non-text files, the LLM **MUST** use the extraction script instead of reading raw bytes:

```bash
python {skill_dir}/scripts/doc_extractor.py "<filepath>"
python {skill_dir}/scripts/doc_extractor.py "<filepath>" --max-pages 50
python {skill_dir}/scripts/doc_extractor.py "<filepath>" --max-rows 10000
```

Where `{skill_dir}` is the directory containing this SKILL.md file.

**Supported formats**:
| Format | Extension | Library | Notes |
|--------|-----------|---------|-------|
| PDF | `.pdf` | PyMuPDF | `sort=True` for reading order, checks encryption |
| Excel | `.xlsx` | openpyxl | `read_only=True, data_only=True` |
| Excel (legacy) | `.xls` | xlrd | For older Excel files |
| Word | `.docx` | python-docx | Preserves headings and tables |
| PowerPoint | `.pptx` | python-pptx | Slides, tables, speaker notes, group shapes |
| RTF | `.rtf` | striprtf | Handles various codepages gracefully |
| EPUB | `.epub` | ebooklib + BeautifulSoup | Spine-ordered chapter extraction |
| OpenDocument Text | `.odt` | odfdo | Paragraphs, tables; markdown conversion fallback |
| OpenDocument Spreadsheet | `.ods` | odfdo | Table extraction with sheet names |
| OpenDocument Presentation | `.odp` | odfdo | Slide text from draw pages |
| Images (OCR) | `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.webp`, `.bmp` | EasyOCR | CJK+EN mixed content, `~ch_sim`+`en` models, paragraph=False |
| SVG | `.svg` | Inline text → svglib+reportlab → OCR fallback | Extract `<text>/<tspan>` elements first, rasterize then OCR if empty |

**Setup** (one-time): Install dependencies. **Use Chinese mirror if default pip timeout:**

```bash
# Try default first
pip install PyMuPDF openpyxl python-docx xlrd python-pptx striprtf ebooklib beautifulsoup4 lxml odfdo paddleocr paddlepaddle svglib reportlab

# If timeout, use Alibaba mirror:
pip install --index-url https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/ --trusted-host mirrors.aliyun.com PyMuPDF openpyxl python-docx xlrd python-pptx striprtf ebooklib beautifulsoup4 lxml odfdo paddleocr paddlepaddle svglib reportlab
```

**⚠️ Note**: First PaddleOCR call takes ~30s to initialize models (cached afterward). Subsequent OCR calls are fast.

**For text files** (.md, .txt, .csv, .json, etc.): Use the Read tool directly — no extraction needed.

```python

## Excel File Workflows

## CRITICAL: Use Formulas, Not Hardcoded Values

**Always use Excel formulas instead of calculating values in Python and hardcoding them.** This ensures the spreadsheet remains dynamic and updateable.

### ❌ WRONG - Hardcoding Calculated Values
```python
# Bad: Calculating in Python and hardcoding result
total = df['Sales'].sum()
sheet['B10'] = total  # Hardcodes 5000

# Bad: Computing growth rate in Python
growth = (df.iloc[-1]['Revenue'] - df.iloc[0]['Revenue']) / df.iloc[0]['Revenue']
sheet['C5'] = growth  # Hardcodes 0.15

# Bad: Python calculation for average
avg = sum(values) / len(values)
sheet['D20'] = avg  # Hardcodes 42.5
```

### ✅ CORRECT - Using Excel Formulas
```python
# Good: Let Excel calculate the sum
sheet['B10'] = '=SUM(B2:B9)'

# Good: Growth rate as Excel formula
sheet['C5'] = '=(C4-C2)/C2'

# Good: Average using Excel function
sheet['D20'] = '=AVERAGE(D2:D19)'
```

This applies to ALL calculations - totals, percentages, ratios, differences, etc. The spreadsheet should be able to recalculate when source data changes.

   - If `status` is `errors_found`, check `error_summary` for specific error types and locations
   - Fix the identified errors and recalculate again
   - Common errors to fix:

     - `#DIV/0!`: Division by zero

     - `#NAME?`: Unrecognized formula name

### Creating new Excel files

2. **短板（一段论述）**：

3. **补缺建议**：

| 项目属性                   | 团队部分调整                                                 |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **学术型项目**（高校主导） | 以学者履历和论文成果为核心，量化H指数、引用数、论文数        |
| **企业型项目**（公司主导） | 以公司资质（知识产权数量/类型、ISO认证、高新企业认证）、客户案例、合作机构列表为核心，团队成员侧重商业履历 |

name: job-description-writer
description: "TRIGGER THIS when crafting job descriptions, posting new roles, defining position requirements, creating hiring briefs, updating JDs, or structuring role expectations. Creates compelling, inclusive, DEI-focused job descriptions with clear requirements, responsibilities, qualifications, salary transparency, and modern hiring language."
---

# Job Description Writer

## Overview
This skill helps HR professionals and hiring managers create effective, inclusive job descriptions that attract diverse talent, clearly communicate role expectations, and support equitable hiring processes. It ensures JDs include comprehensive role details, transparent compensation guidance, DEI language, and compliance-ready structure.

## When to Use This Skill
- Creating new job descriptions for open positions
- Revising existing JDs to be more inclusive or accurate
- Developing hiring briefs for recruiter guidance
- Standardizing JD format across the organization
- Adding salary transparency and DEI elements to existing descriptions
- Ensuring JDs comply with accessibility and non-discrimination standards
- Creating role family templates for similar positions

## Key Components

### 1. Core Structure Template
A well-organized JD should follow this proven framework:
- **Position Title** - Use inclusive, searchable language
- **Department & Reporting Line** - Clear organizational context
- **Position Summary** - 2-3 sentence overview of purpose
- **Key Responsibilities** - 5-8 main duties with impact metrics
- **Required Qualifications** - Only non-negotiable requirements (avoid "nice-to-haves")
- **Preferred Qualifications** - Open doors for diverse candidates
- **Compensation & Benefits** - Transparent salary bands, benefits overview
- **Company Culture/DEI Statement** - Commitment to inclusion
- **Application Instructions** - Accessibility accommodations offered

### 2. Inclusive Language Practices
- Replace "native English speaker" with "fluent in English"
- Use "years of experience" instead of "young and energetic"
- Avoid gendered terms (use "salesperson" not "salesman")
- Include "and more" in job duties to signal flexibility
- Emphasize "equivalent experience" to accept diverse backgrounds
- Replace ageist language (avoid "digital native," "rockstar," "ninja")
- Use "we encourage applications from underrepresented groups"

### 3. Responsibilities Writing
Each responsibility should follow the ACTION-IMPACT format:
- Start with action verb (design, develop, lead, analyze, coordinate)
- Include what you'll do and what business outcome results
- Example: "Lead cross-functional product team to deliver 3 major releases annually, impacting 50,000+ users"
- Quantify impact where possible (X% improvement, $X revenue, X users affected)
- Show growth potential and learning opportunities

### 4. Qualifications Strategy
- **Required**: Only list absolute deal-breakers (certifications, licenses, security clearance)
- **Preferred**: Use this section generously for nice-to-haves
- **Equivalent Experience**: Always include phrases like "or X years of related experience"
- **Skills Over Credentials**: Emphasize transferable skills, not just degree requirements
- Remove unnecessary credential inflation (many jobs don't truly need a 4-year degree)

### 5. Compensation Transparency
Current best practice requires including:
- Base salary range (when possible; check local legal requirements)
- Equity information (if applicable)
- Benefits highlights (healthcare, PTO, retirement, remote options)
- Total compensation approach
- Example format: "$95,000 - $145,000 based on experience and location"
- Note: Some regions require salary transparency; verify local laws

### 6. DEI & Belonging Statements
Include one or more of these elements:
- "We are an Equal Opportunity Employer"
- "We actively encourage applications from people of color, women, LGBTQ+ individuals, people with disabilities, and other underrepresented groups"
- "Accommodations available for candidates with disabilities"
- "We consider experience outside traditional pathways"
- "We provide [specific accommodations] to support your interview process"

### 7. Red Flags to Remove
- Unnecessary years of experience requirements (often exclude capable candidates)
- Gendered or ageist language
- Unclear or vague responsibilities
- "Multitasking" (most jobs involve multiple tasks; show what matters)
- "Startup mentality" or "willing to wear many hats" (exploitative language)
- Unrealistic "must-have" lists that exclude most candidates
- Passive language ("responsible for" instead of action verbs)

## Workflow

### Step 1: Gather Role Information
Interview hiring manager about:
- Core mission of the role
- Key metrics for success
- Team structure and reporting relationships
- Biggest challenges the person will face
- Growth/advancement opportunities
- Current skills gaps on team (to inform requirements)
- Budget, timeline, and hiring urgency

### Step 2: Structure Responsibilities
- List 5-8 primary responsibilities
- Rank by importance and time allocation
- Convert to action-impact statements
- Add success metrics where applicable
- Group related duties for clarity

### Step 3: Define Qualifications
- Separate true requirements from nice-to-haves
- Include equivalent experience language
- Highlight transferable skills
- Remove credential inflation
- Consider diverse pathways to the role

### Step 4: Build Inclusive Elements
- Review language for bias
- Add DEI statement appropriate to company values
- Include accessibility accommodations
- Check that role appeals to broad talent pools
- Verify compensation transparency compliance

### Step 5: Finalize & Review
- Read aloud for tone and clarity
- Ensure action verbs throughout
- Verify no discriminatory language
- Check for internal consistency
- Get manager approval before posting

## Template Example

```
POSITION TITLE: Senior Product Manager, Financial Services

DEPARTMENT: Product Management | Reports to: VP of Product

POSITION SUMMARY
Lead the design, development, and launch of innovative financial services products that serve our customer base of 500,000+ small businesses. You'll partner closely with engineering, design, and go-to-market teams to deliver products that are secure, intuitive, and compliant with regulatory requirements.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
- Lead the full product lifecycle for 2-3 financial services products from concept through post-launch, defining roadmaps that balance user needs, business objectives, and regulatory requirements
- Conduct market research and user research (quarterly) to understand customer pain points, inform feature prioritization, and validate product-market fit assumptions
- Collaborate with Engineering and Design to define product requirements, acceptance criteria, and success metrics; conduct code reviews and design reviews to ensure quality
- Own go-to-market strategy and launch execution for new products, including positioning, pricing, marketing strategy, and sales enablement
- Analyze product metrics and customer feedback; report quarterly on KPIs and iterate on strategy based on data insights
- Build and maintain cross-functional relationships with Finance, Legal, and Compliance to navigate regulatory requirements for financial services
- Mentor and develop 1-2 junior product managers; provide feedback and coaching on decision-making and stakeholder management

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
- 5+ years of product management experience
- Experience shipping at least 2 products (from concept through launch)
- Strong analytical skills; proficiency with SQL, analytics tools, or data visualization
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- Ability to influence without direct authority

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
- Experience in fintech, financial services, or heavily regulated industries
- Background in user research or design thinking methodologies
- Management experience and coaching of dir

name: evomind-paper-scan
description: OpenClaw-compatible EvoMind skill for academic paper quality review, 29-dimension paper audit, source-data/table numeric scanning with paperconan attribution, bilingual reporting, and professional Word DOCX internal review reports.
---

# EvoMind Paper Scan

`evomind-paper-scan` is an OpenClaw-compatible academic review skill. It combines:

- whole-paper 29-dimension quality review;
- paper/source-data/table consistency review;
- numeric anomaly scanning for data tables using `paperconan`;
- cautious research-integrity risk language;
- EvoMind-branded Markdown and Word internal reports.

## Branding and Attribution

Use these exact defaults unless the user overrides them:

- Overall review process: `EvoMind Paper-Data-Scan v1.0（EvoMind 自研审查流程）`
- Review institution: `EvoMind 学术质量审查实验室`
- Document number: `EM-REP-20260602-001`
- Confidentiality: `内部资料`
- Header: `EvoMind 内部审查报告`
- Footer: `EvoMind 学术质量审查实验室 | 内部资料`
- Sign-off warning: `AI判断不能作为最终结果，需人工复核`

Data audit attribution is mandatory:

> 数据审核/数字异常扫描部分使用 paperconan 开源工具，项目地址：https://github.com/zixixr/paperconan。EvoMind 尊重并保留原作者工具署名；EvoMind Paper-Data-Scan v1.0 指本机构的整合审查流程、报告规范和人工复核框架。

Do not describe `paperconan` as EvoMind self-developed. EvoMind owns the integrated review workflow and report format, while the data numeric scan component must credit paperconan.

## Required Review Order

1. Confirm inputs: paper PDF/DOCX, source-data folder, supplementary files, desired language, and output folder.
2. Read the whole paper first. Identify title, author/year, field, research question, methods, tables, figures, claims, datasets, and source-data availability.
3. Complete the 29-dimension review using `references/29-dimension-checklist.md`.
4. Build a figure/table/source-data review queue.
5. Run numeric scan on source-data/supplementary tables when available. Use paperconan and preserve attribution.
6. Interpret numeric findings only through paper text, captions, methods, sample structure, and plausible benign explanations. Never treat scanner severity as final judgment.
7. Produce Markdown reports, auxiliary summaries, and a DOCX internal report if requested.

## Direct Script Usage

From the skill folder:

```powershell
python .\scripts\run_evomind_paper_scan.py --paper "<paper.pdf>" --source-data "<source data folder>" --out-dir ".\reports" --title "<paper title>" --docx
```

If no source-data folder exists, omit `--source-data`; the script will scan the PDF table extraction where possible and mark source data as missing.

The script creates:

```text
reports/
  <paper-title>/
    paper_data_scan_zh.md
    paper_data_scan_en.md
    auxiliary/
      numeric_scan_summary_zh.md
      numeric_scan_summary_en.md
      source_data_inventory_zh.md
      source_data_inventory_en.md
    audit/
      scan.json
      REPORT.md
      report.html
    EvoMind_内部审查报告.docx
```

## Output Rules

The main report must include:

- report metadata and EvoMind branding;
- paper identity and reviewed files;
- whole-paper baseline;
- 29-dimension quality matrix;
- source-data inventory;
- numeric scan summary with paperconan attribution;
- integrated findings comparing paper text, tables, figures, source data, and scanner output;
- limitations and next manual checks;
- red sign-off warning in DOCX.

## Integrity Language

Never conclude misconduct, fraud, fabrication, plagiarism, or author intent from scanner output alone. Use language such as:

- `possible fabrication risk`;
- `requires raw data confirmation`;
- `confirmed inconsistency`;
- `scanner finding with plausible benign explanation`;
- `source data unavailable, reproducibility limited`.

## Related Files

- `OPENCLAW.md`: OpenClaw installation and usage guide.
- `skill.yaml`: OpenClaw package metadata.
- `security.json`: local-only permissions and data-handling policy.
- `scripts/run_evomind_paper_scan.py`: direct runnable pipeline.
- `scripts/generate_evomind_word_report.py`: DOCX generator.
- `references/29-dimension-checklist.md`: required review matrix.
- `references/numeric-scan-interpretation.md`: scanner interpretation guardrails.
